criteria.justification: The response explicitly states 'The decision is not whether to follow the company's platform strategy. It is whether to put a broader migration on the critical path for this launch,' cleanly separating the two questions.

It grounds the recommendation in the technically-derived estimate, stating 'Treating the optimistic timeline as the plan would mean accepting delivery risk without evidence that the underlying gaps can be closed faster.'

The response only notes that extending the old platform 'creates some additional work on a retiring platform,' which is a cost/debt framing, but it never discusses the risk of inconsistent customer experience across products from having some traffic on the old platform and some on the new.

It directly frames the recommendation as 'preserving the strategic destination while declining to make this launch depend on an inadequately buffered migration,' and invites leadership to make an explicit trade-off decision rather than assume the optimistic timeline, addressing the optics of appearing to resist company direction.

The response commits to a specific recommendation (extend the old platform, treat migration as a separate owned effort) and lays out three concrete execution safeguards, including assigning an owner and setting a planning milestone.
